text: In 2020-03 we converged on a name. One hundred five of us said "the cares act," and the record marks its first appearance at 2019-04-23, first said by S001207. Around it we assembled the longer phrasing in near-identical counts: "relief and economic," ninety-six of us; "aid relief and economic," ninety-five; "relief and economic security," ninety-four. Ninety-three of us said "coronavirus aid relief and economic," and ninety-three "aid relief and economic security." Ninety-one reached the full "coronavirus aid relief and economic security," while eighty-eight said "the coronavirus aid relief and economic." The counts descend by ones and twos as the phrase lengthens, each of us dropping off a word later than the last. We peaked together on 2020-03-27. We were reciting the title of a bill, and we recited it almost to the word.
